The Process

How it works.

You install Archie, build an agent, and message it from anywhere: no code, no config files, no terminal. Here’s the whole picture, one step at a time.

The handover

What handing something over looks like.

You message your agent the way you’d text a friend (“what’s on my calendar?” “move my 3 o’clock,” “catch me up on today’s meetings”). It goes away and works, comes back if it needs you, and tells you when it’s done.

Your agent holds the things you’d otherwise carry in your head. Tell it once: the follow-up on Friday, the detail to check before the call. It messages you first when the time comes.

Not all of it is work to hand over. Ask how to word a hard email, or what to cook with what is in the fridge, and your agent answers the way any AI chat you have used does, in the same conversation.

What Archie hands you

A file on your computer, not text to copy out.

Ask Archie for a spreadsheet and your agent writes a file on your computer, then tells you where it put it.

The list is an allowlist, so anything not on it cannot be written at all, and every kind on it is inert: opening one shows text or a table, and none of them is something your computer runs on a double click. How that is kept safe →

The moving parts

How it all connects.

Your agent runs on your own computer, built from a handful of parts you choose. Here is the whole thing, everywhere it reaches, and the one place it waits.

When it thinks, it talks to the AI company directly, on your account, never through us. One exception, and it is ours: the free starter credits and the plan with the AI included reach Anthropic through a server of ours. It sends email and changes your calendar only after you approve each one, and it can’t spend money. See how we prove it →

The whole list

What you actually need.

Less than you’d think. Three things, and you probably have one of them already. A chat app makes four, and that one can wait.

1

A computer that stays on and connected

One you don’t mind leaving powered on, awake and online: your agent can only answer while Archie is running. Use the one you have. A laptop needs to stay plugged in and set never to sleep, and we’ll sort that with you. Buying for it? A Mac mini is the easy answer, and the picker below settles it for your situation.

Archie runs on both Mac and Windows.

2

AI usage, on your account or ours

The account bills you for what your agent does, pay-as-you-go: $1 to $5 a month for a handful of tasks a day, up to around $140 for one wired into a whole working day, capped by you and never seen by us. Worked out for 3 levels of use. Free tiers differ, and Google’s is the one Google trains on: what each company does with your words, before you pick.

You can start with eligible free credits instead, for 14 days. Personal also offers AI-included usage at launch; both routes use our server and need your own key for email and text reading. Limits and prices.

3

An Otian account, which costs nothing to make

Archie asks you to sign in when it opens, and a browser window handles it. The account itself is free, and so is Archie on an AI account of your own: 20 jobs a day, where a job is one piece of work, a reply to you or a routine running or an email it reacts to. At launch a plan takes that limit off at $30 a month or $299 a year, and runs up to ten agents. On our side we hold your email address, license and listed operational records. Never a conversation.

On your own AI key, the app and AI usage are separate bills, and on the free tier only the second one exists. Every cost, in full.

+

Optional: a chat app, to be reached anywhere

Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix or, on a Mac, iMessage. Your agent lives there like a contact, the same conversation from your desk or your phone. Nothing to sort out before you start, though: you can talk to it inside Archie itself. Telegram is the quickest.

On a Mac, iMessage needs no account at all. WhatsApp is the one still missing: it does not let an app like this answer on your behalf, its rule and not our choice. Either way, what your agent tells you crosses that company’s servers, so we are building Archie Mobile.

Which computer

Answer a few questions and we’ll lay out your kit.

Nothing you answer here leaves your browser.

Your kit Question 1
Save your money

What you don’t need.

A page recommending equipment has an obvious incentive to make the list longer. This is the other list, with the reasons.

Not needed

  • A good graphics card. The thinking happens on your AI company’s computers, not yours. Whatever is in the computer already is enough
  • A fast or new computer. It spends most of its life idle, waiting for something to happen
  • A server, a NAS, or anything in a rack. Archie is a desktop app with a window
  • A second monitor, or any monitor after setup. You need a screen to set it up, and after that your phone will do
  • A separate internet connection, or a static address. Nothing connects to your computer: it reaches out, and nothing on the network can reach in

Worth having

  • An Ethernet cable, if the computer can sit near the router
  • Disk space, if you want it to talk out loud or work with audio and video: those tools run on your computer
  • A power strip with battery backup, if your power flickers. The difference between a blip and a computer that stays off until you come home
  • A phone, which you have. It is how you reach the agent when you are not at the computer

No hardware prices here: we would be quoting somebody else’s, and it would be wrong within the month. Every computer named above is one you can price at the maker’s own store.

Setup

Your path to a running agent.

5 steps from a quiet computer to an agent you can message from anywhere, and one promise for whatever comes after.

  1. 01

    Pick a computer your agent can live on

    Everything your agent needs is above.

  2. 02

    Install the Archie desktop app

    One download, then sign in. Archie is in testing, and the waitlist hears the day Archie opens. See where Archie stands →

  3. 03

    Meet your agent

    Name it and answer a few questions. It fits itself out from your answers, tells you what it added, and you can take any of it back off. Browse the marketplace when you want more.

  4. 04

    Connect your chat app

    Your agent gets its own account on the chat app you picked, and you message it the way you would message a person.

  5. 05

    Message your agent from anywhere

    Archie does the work on your computer and replies in your chat. Email and calendar changes wait for your approval, every one.

  6. 06

    Hit a ceiling? Tell us

    If Archie can’t do it yet, we build the add-on, and every commissioned add-on becomes a marketplace listing.

2 ways in

On your own, or with us beside you.

You can do all of this yourself, at your own pace, with every add-on included. Guided setup is for everyone who’d rather not: a free call first, then we build it with you over screen share. What a session involves →
